html:
From 1928 to 1956 India won the men's hockey gold medal at six Olympic Games in a row. It was the first field in which Indians, still under British rule, were plainly the best in the world.

The British army brought hockey to India, and it took root in army towns and railway colonies. India first sent a team to the Games at Amsterdam in 1928. It won the gold without letting in a goal.

Its star was Dhyan Chand, a soldier from Jhansi who had learnt the game by practising at night after duty. In Los Angeles in 1932 India beat the United States 24 to 1. In Berlin in 1936, with Hitler's government watching, it beat Germany 8 to 1 in the final. Dhyan Chand scored three of the goals.

The first Games after independence were in London in 1948. India beat Great Britain 4 to 0 in the final at Wembley, a win that meant more at home than any other. Golds followed in 1952 and 1956. The run ended in 1960 with a loss to Pakistan, by then the great rival. India won again in 1964 and 1980, eight golds in all.

Artificial pitches, introduced in the 1970s, suited a faster style, and cricket took hockey's place in Indian hearts (see the 1983 World Cup).
sum: From 1928 to 1956 India won the men's hockey gold medal at six Olympic Games in a row. It was the first field in which Indians, still under British rule, were plainly the best in the world.
